newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria oil refinery quits links with trade firms.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria oil refinery quits links with trade firms.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved on Thursday a decision of the Neftohim oil refinery to quit its participation in nine Bulgarian trade firms and a bank to ease the plant's financial crisis, government officials said.
"The aim is to release Neftohim's financial resources because of the refinery's financial crisis," said a senior government official, after the cabinet's closed meeting.

He said that the bank was the Bulgarian-Russian Investment Bank in Sofia and among the trade firms was an International Management Centre in Sofia, Biochem Sofia and DSO Himsnab, which is a chain of shops in Sofia.

Local financial weekly newspaper Kapital said the plant owed more than $200 million to some of its crude suppliers. Part of the debt is a result from a barter deal of the refinery carried out at the order of the Socialist government.
The refinery exported 50,000 tonnes of fuel to Yugoslavia against grain and has received by the Bulgarian government only two billion levs instead $69 million, Kapital said.
Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery at the Black Sea port of Bourgas agreed last week to increase its workers' wages by 35 percent from January 1 to avert a threatened strike.

Neftohim officials say the refinery has suffered huge losses because of the drastic collapse of the lev, forcing up the cost of imported crude faster than the rise in Neftohim's domestic sales prices.
The government usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
The Bulgarian lev traded near 900 per dollar on Thursday amid expectations of a further fall.
